result_text:
`repair_default_enum_values(schema)` now exists and is exported from `ariadne`, and `validate_schema_enum_values` was already exported. The full test suite gives 9 failed and 615 passed. All 9 failures are in the asgi websocket and configuration tests. A run with my changes stashed gave 11 failed and 613 passed, so those tests were already failing, though I didn't compare the two sets of failing tests.

`repair_default_enum_values` walks every object and interface field argument, every input field and every directive argument. Where a default is declared in the schema, it recomputes the default from that declaration. That puts the bound Python value (for example the `Enum` member) where graphql-core had put a string. It handles list and nested-object defaults too. I didn't write tests for it, as instructed.

`make_executable_schema` now calls the new function and no longer calls `set_default_enum_values_on_schema`. I removed the old private `repair_default_enum_values(schema, bindables)` helper from `ariadne/executable_schema.py`. The new function is in `ariadne/enums.py`.

I left `set_default_enum_values_on_schema` in place and still exported. The issue only said it could be dropped, and removing a public function would break anyone importing it.

`EnumType.bind_to_default_values` is also still there, now unused by `make_executable_schema`.

I didn't update `CHANGELOG.md`.
